You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
A government decides that all non-essential businesses must close for three months due to a disease pandemic. What is an opportunity cost of this policy?

options.A: increased leisure time for employees
options.B: lives that are saved due to reduced disease levels
options.C: the production of goods by essential businesses
options.D: the loss of goods from the closed businesses

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an economy’s production possibility curve. The economy produces combinations of goods and services using all available resources. services O goods What does the production possibility curve indicate for goods and services?

options.A: constant returns to scale in the production of both goods and services
options.B: diminishing returns to scale in the production of both goods and services
options.C: increasing returns to scale in the production of both goods and services
options.D: infinite returns to scale in the production of both goods and services

questions.questionText: Which economic conditions are likely to encourage an increase in enterprise? consumer interest rates profit tax unemployment confidence

options.A: high high high high
options.B: high low low high
options.C: low low high low
options.D: low low low low

questions.questionText: When is the price elasticity of demand for a product most likely to be price elastic?

options.A: A large percentage of income is spent on the product.
options.B: It is measured in the short run.
options.C: It is a necessity product.
options.D: There are few substitutes available.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to cause a shift in the supply curve for rice?

options.A: a change in the price of the rice
options.B: a change in the price of meat
options.C: a change in the size of the rice industry
options.D: a change in tastes and preferences for rice

questions.questionText: A free market is in disequilibrium with a shortage of a product. As the market moves towards equilibrium, what will happen to the price, the quantity demanded and the quantity supplied? quantity quantity price demanded supplied

options.A: decrease decrease increase
options.B: decrease increase decrease
options.C: increase decrease increase
options.D: increase increase decrease

questions.questionText: What would not cause a shift in the demand curve for a good?

options.A: a change in the price of a complement
options.B: a change in the price of a substitute
options.C: a change in the price of the good itself
options.D: a change in consumers’ incomes

questions.questionText: What does joint supply mean?

options.A: A firm can choose between producing a range of different goods.
options.B: A good has multiple uses.
options.C: A good is a by-product of the production process of another good.
options.D: Consumers consider two goods as complements.

questions.questionText: When the price of a firm’s product falls by 5%, its total revenue also falls by 5%. What describes the product’s price elasticity of demand?

options.A: elastic
options.B: infinite
options.C: unitary
options.D: zero

questions.questionText: The table shows how an individual’s weekly consumption of biscuits and coffee varies with income. income biscuits coffee ($) (packs) (cups) 100 0 5 150 5 10 Which statement about the income elasticity of demand over the range of income shown is correct?

options.A: For biscuits it is greater than 1.
options.B: For biscuits it is zero.
options.C: For coffee it is less than 1.
options.D: For coffee it is unitary.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows four supply curves. W X price Y Z O quantity Which statement about the price elasticity of these supply curves is correct?

options.A: W has elasticity of 0 that will rise as price rises.
options.B: X has elasticity greater than 1 that will be constant as price rises.
options.C: Y has elasticity greater than 1 that will fall as price rises.
options.D: Z has elasticity of 0 that is constant as quantity rises.

questions.questionText: Product X has a price elasticity of supply (PES) of +2, whilst product Y has a PES of +0.2. Which statement about products X and Y is correct?

options.A: X has more substitutes than Y.
options.B: A 20% price fall would lead to a greater decrease in production of Y than of X.
options.C: After a price rise, it is more difficult to increase Y’s output than X’s.
options.D: After a price fall of 10%, more people would buy X than would buy Y.

questions.questionText: There are 10000 tickets available to watch a sports final at a national stadium. The initial market equilibrium ticket price is $20. The government decides to fix an effective minimum price for the tickets. Under which conditions will the consumer surplus for the tickets decrease the most as a result of the minimum price? minimum price elasticity price level of demand $ for tickets

The diagram shows the impact of a government imposing a unit tax on a demerit good. S is the supply curve before the tax and S is the supply curve after the tax. price $ S S D 0 5 10 quantity What is the after-tax revenue of the firm producing the demerit good?

A government has a policy aim of reducing income inequality. It considers three policies. Which combination of policies would be most effective? a subsidy on an increase in the an increase in the battery-powered marginal rate of tax minimum wage cars which cost from 40% to 50% over $40000

options.A: yes no no
options.B: yes yes no
options.C: yes no yes
options.D: no yes no

questions.questionText: A Bangladeshi citizen is employed as a construction worker in Qatar. He sends some of his wages to his family in Bangladesh. How will this be recorded on Qatar’s balance of payments?

options.A: as part of the balance of trade in services
options.B: as part of net primary income
options.C: as part of net secondary income
options.D: as part of the financial account

questions.questionText: The table gives data for an economy. 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) 200 220 240 300 320 at current prices ($ billion) GDP deflator (price index) 100 109 125 149 154 In which year did real GDP decline compared with the previous year?
Which policy is most likely to help to correct an adverse balance on the current account of the balance of payments?

options.A: abolishing tariffs
options.B: depreciating the currency
options.C: reducing direct taxes
options.D: reducing indirect taxes

questions.questionText: In year 1, a country’s real GDP was $500 billion. In year 2, nominal GDP rose to $577.5 billion and the prices increased by 5%. What is the real GDP in year 2?

options.A: $4.76 billion B $5 billion C $476 billion D $550 billion

questions.questionText: The table gives details of national income statistics for an economy. US$bn consumption 2000 investment 500 government expenditure 600 net exports –100 net foreign factor income –200 depreciation 100 What is the net national income for this economy?

options.A: US$2700bn B US$2800bn C US$2900bn D US$3000bn

questions.questionText: The table shows the relative price of exports compared with imports expressed as an index number for an economy (2013 = 100). date index 2013 100 2014 97 2015 95 Which statement about the period 2013–2015 is correct?

options.A: Export prices have increased each year.
options.B: The general level of prices has fallen.
options.C: The terms of trade have deteriorated.
options.D: The volume of imports increasingly exceeds the volume of exports.

questions.questionText: Country X and country Y each allocate half of their resources towards the manufacturing of shoes, and the other half towards the manufacturing of t-shirts. Resources can be used equally effectively in the production of both products in both countries. The table shows the output of shoes and t-shirts produced by both countries using half their resources in each case, before specialisation. country shoes t-shirts X 4000 12000 Y 2000 8000 total 6000 20000 What can be concluded from the data?

options.A: The opportunity cost of country Y producing two shoes is four t-shirts.
options.B: The opportunity cost of country X producing one t-shirt is four shoes.
options.C: The total output of shoes and t-shirts after specialisation would be 24000.
options.D: The total output of shoes and t-shirts after specialisation would be 28000.

questions.questionText: Which government action is least likely to prevent a fall in economic growth?

options.A: additional controls on commercial banks’ lending
options.B: relaxation of rules for immigration of adult population
options.C: removal of trade barriers on import of raw materials
options.D: training and education of workforce

questions.questionText: What is the most likely cause of an outward shift of a country’s aggregate demand curve?

options.A: a decrease in the competitiveness of domestically produced products
options.B: a decrease in the general price level
options.C: a decrease in the money supply
options.D: a depreciation of the country’s exchange rate

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the macroeconomic equilibrium output and price level changing from Y and P to Y and P .
A country had a current account surplus of $141bn. Which policy may its government implement to reduce this surplus in the short run?

options.A: a decrease in direct taxes
options.B: a decrease in regulations to encourage more foreign firms to locate in this country
options.C: an increase of import duties
options.D: an increase in interest rates

questions.questionText: The diagram shows aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply in the short run (SRAS) and the long run (LRAS). LRAS LRAS price level W SRAS SRAS Y AD O real GDP Which row is correct in causing a shift in the short run aggregate supply from SRAS to SRAS and the long run aggregate supply from LRAS to LRAS ? shift from SRAS to SRAS shift from LRAS to LRAS

The diagram shows that the imposition of a tariff raises a product’s world price from $10 to $14. domestic supply price $ domestic demand 0 20 30 70 100 quantity (millions) By how much did domestic producers’ income increase as a result of the tariff?

options.A: $120 million B $160 million C $220 million D $280 million

questions.questionText: Which approach would a government be most likely to use to eliminate deflation?

options.A: an increase in direct taxes
options.B: an increase in interest rates
options.C: a reduction in indirect taxes
